events.summary: Anthropic launched the 'Anthropic Cyber Mission'. Palo Alto Networks is one of 11 founding partners of its Critical Infrastructure Defense Program, which gives frontier Claude models, on-site engineers and threat research to security providers defending power grids, water systems, transport networks and government systems. The other partners include CrowdStrike, Accenture, Booz Allen, Deloitte, Dragos, Hitachi, Insane Cyber, Nozomi Networks, PwC and Rockwell Automation. Palo Alto's quoted line: 'By combining Unit 42 threat intelligence and operational expertise with Anthropic's frontier models, we're helping operators defend against adversaries.' No financial terms were disclosed.
events.why_it_matters: Thesis 2 (AI creates new things to protect): a top AI lab chose Palo Alto (and CrowdStrike) as a partner. But it carries no disclosed revenue, so it is a signal of relevance, not a sales number. The stock fell on Thursday, so there is no visible price reaction.

events.summary: Lee Klarich (EVP, Chief Product & Technology Officer, and director): his family trust (the Lee and Susan Klarich 2005 Trust) gave away 60,000 shares on 2026-10-08 (Form 4 code G, price $0, not under a 10b5-1 plan). After it, the trust holds 555,070 shares and he holds 235,983 directly (791,053 total), so the gift was about 7.05% of his reported holdings (our calculation). The Form 144 filed the same evening shows the receiver: the Boost Giving Foundation, a charitable 501(c)(3) organization founded by Klarich 'of which Mr. Klarich controls investment decisions', planned to sell 60,000 shares through Goldman Sachs around 2026-10-08, aggregate market value $23,910,000 (= $398.50 a share, Thursday's close). The 144 lists no 10b5-1 plan adoption date and no sales in the past three months. 60,000 shares is about 0.0073% of the 818 million shares outstanding stated in the 144. This repeats a pattern: he gave 25,000 shares on 2026-09-30 (already in the news log).
events.why_it_matters: Economically this is a charitable donation followed by the charity selling the shares, not Klarich cashing out for himself; a Form 144 is a notice of a planned sale, and no Form 4 confirms the foundation's actual sale. Small against his holdings and the company. Relevant to the 'several insiders sold outside 10b5-1 plans' check (see thesis_breaker_checks).

products.name: Anthropic Critical Infrastructure Defense Program (Palo Alto as founding partner, through Unit 42)
products.what_it_is: A program in which Anthropic gives its most capable Claude AI models, on-site engineers and threat research to a small group of security companies that protect power grids, water systems, transport networks and government systems. Palo Alto contributes Unit 42, its threat-intelligence and incident-response team.
products.analogy: Like a top research lab lending its best equipment and scientists to a few fire brigades that protect the city's power plants and water works.
products.buyers: The end customers are operators of critical infrastructure (utilities, water, transport) and governments; they buy security from the partners. Whether money flows between Anthropic and Palo Alto is not disclosed.
products.how_it_works: Partners combine Anthropic's frontier models with their own threat data and know-how to find and stop attacks on operational technology (the computers that run physical equipment) faster. Work is 'underway'; expansion is planned 'over the coming months'.
products.sales: not disclosed (Anthropic's announcement contains no financial terms)
products.sales_source: Proxy: none specific. Company-wide, next-generation security ARR was $9.10bn at Q4 FY2026 (PANW Q4 FY2026 results, 2026-09-01); the program's share of it is unknown.
products.size_for_company: unknown; no revenue attached to the announcement
products.competition: CrowdStrike is a fellow founding partner; OT-security specialists Dragos and Nozomi Networks and consultancies (Accenture, Booz Allen, Deloitte, PwC) are also in the program.
products.why_investors_care: Evidence for Thesis 2: a leading AI lab picked Palo Alto as a partner for AI-era defence. It is a relevance signal, not yet sales.
products.watch_next: Whether Palo Alto gives any customer, ARR or revenue figure for AI-security work on the Q1 FY2027 call (pillar 3).
